PullRequest.Title: sessions: apply custom group colors to names
PullRequest.Body:

Applies a group's assigned color to its name as well as its icon, making customized groups easier to distinguish from sessions. Name colors adapt for readable contrast on normal and hovered rows; keyboard focus, selection, high-contrast themes, and translucent shell backgrounds keep their standard foregrounds.

This is a color-only change. Indentation, hierarchy guides, group organization, and existing settings are unchanged.

To try it, use **Change Icon/Color** on a custom group or a workspace, repository, or environment group. Change and reset its color, then check hover, selection, and theme changes in default and compact layouts.

Headless component-fixture previews from [Screenshots & Tests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/42315987589):

| Light, default layout | Light, compact layout |
| --- | --- |
| The assigned blue identifies Release work; other names are unchanged. | The hovered group retains its color; keyboard focus keeps the standard foreground. |
| ![Assigned group name color in the light default layout](https://hediet-screenshots.azurewebsites.net/images/0fb0661e8c9df671a0ca1a43989295ec042347205068ebbb33ae8b79e83f95c0) | ![Colored hover and standard keyboard focus in the light compact layout](https://hediet-screenshots.azurewebsites.net/images/4f4846caabd2777e4d0e7481e7d38b1921ca70a96a87585ed5de725b38707e0b) |

Validation:
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` — passed.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\test\browser\sessionsList.test.ts --reporter dot` — 462 passed.
- Targeted TypeScript ESLint and CSS lint — passed; CSS lint reported three existing advisory design-token suggestions.
- Eight default/compact Light, Dark, and high-contrast fixtures — passed render/dispose and remount-stability checks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or scroll the Sessions list with custom-colored groups, workspace sections, repository sections, or environment sections
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For each colored header template that enters the rendered viewport, renderSessionHeaderIcon synchronously constructs SessionHeaderLabelColor; its constructor resolves three theme colors, computes normal and hover contrast, and writes one class plus two CSS custom properties before the row paint can complete.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the effective number of simultaneously rendered colored headers, including a possible sticky-header copy, rather than all stored groups; WorkbenchObjectTree virtualizes off-screen rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All contrast calculations and DOM writes run serially on the UI thread during row rendering; there is no queue, parallelism, or asynchronous boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no shared contrast cache. A warm template rerender disposes the prior instance/listener and recomputes the two colors, while off-screen templates retain no SessionHeaderLabelColor. Theme color lookup itself is in-memory.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the constructor call, synchronous updateStyles call, virtualized renderer lifecycle, and disposal through elementDisposables are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact viewport/header counts and rerender frequency vary, but each unit performs only bounded color arithmetic and three style/class mutations; realistic visible cardinality is bounded by the viewport.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded synchronous work per visible colored header, but does not force layout, scan an unbounded collection, retain off-screen listeners, or cross an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch the active color theme while colored Sessions headers are visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing theme service synchronously notifies one newly added Themable listener per rendered colored header; each listener recomputes two contrast colors and updates that header's class and CSS properties before the theme update settles.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fan-out scales with currently rendered colored header templates, including sticky copies, not the total session/group history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Theme listeners execute serially on the UI thread; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each header recomputes on a theme change because the background, hover background, and selected custom color can all change. Disposing or recycling a row unregisters its listener, so there is no stale-listener accumulation across scrolling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: Themable registers onDidColorThemeChange, and both section/group renderers clear elementDisposables on rerender and disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Theme changes are user-driven and infrequent; the precise number of visible customized headers varies, but virtualization bounds it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new fan-out is bounded to live rendered headers and performs small in-memory arithmetic plus DOM writes without layout reads or retained-growth behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Assign or reset a group/section color from the Sessions header context menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the picker returns a color, the existing setGroupColor/setSectionColor path serializes and stores group state, emits onDidChange, rebuilds the visible list, and the changed renderer additionally computes and applies label contrast for rendered colored headers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build the complete serialized session-group state, JSON.stringify it, and store it in profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one serialization/profile-storage call for a changed accepted color; zero when the selected value equals the existing value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Changing an icon color already used the same setter/save/event path and full-state serialization; this diff changes label rendering after that event but does not add or multiply the storage boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence occurs synchronously before the change event drives the visible list update.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One persistence operation occurs per accepted color change. Serialization scales with the existing group, membership, section-appearance, and child-order state; the added label work scales only with rendered colored headers after the update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The setter, JSON serialization, storage call, list update, and header styling execute synchronously/serially in the existing event path; no burst or new concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repeatedly selecting the identical color is suppressed by existing equality checks. Reset removes the appearance and the rerender disposes the label-color object/listener; no negative or stale cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the picker callbacks, setters, save implementation, onDidChange handler, and render path are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Stored state can vary in size, but this PR does not change its serialized cardinality or write frequency; added label styling remains viewport-bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only persistence/serialization boundary is pre-existing and unchanged; the diff adds bounded in-memory/UI work after the existing update.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and all diff hunks. Traced production row rendering, theme-change fan-out, renderer cleanup, color-change persistence, virtualization, cache behavior, and effective concurrency. The added per-header contrast work is bounded to rendered templates and correctly disposed; no actionable diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
